#55435. Senior Analytics Engineer at Kit

Senior Analytics Engineer at Kit

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love.
  • Recent findings suggest that our Sales team needs a dedicated data partner, and creator commerce (how creators monetize by selling digital products) is becoming a bigger part of how Kit and our creators scale.
  • Sources indicate that accurate sales data gives our team a clear picture of the pipeline and the confidence to make informed decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

Recent findings suggest that our Sales team needs a dedicated data partner, and creator commerce (how creators monetize by selling digital products) is becoming a bigger part of how Kit and our creators scale. Kit is growing, so we're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to own Kit's sales and commerce data from end to end.

Sources indicate that accurate sales data gives our team a clear picture of the pipeline and the confidence to make informed decisions. That’s what makes this role so important.

Sources indicate that your primary focus will be Sales: the dbt models that turn our CRM data into trusted pipeline, deal, and funnel metrics, and the Omni dashboards our sales leader and Senior Revenue Operations Manager use to run the business. You'll also model creator commerce data, so we understand what creators sell and earn through Kit, and you'll pick up reporting work with our Product team, such as feature usage reporting. On a small data team, we step outside our usual lanes when the need is there, so the mix will shift over time.

According to recent reports, you'll build for two kinds of consumers: people and AI. Teammates increasingly answer their own questions by querying our semantic layer through Omni's AI and MCP connections to AI tools. That means your models, metric definitions, and documentation need to be clear and correct enough for an AI agent to use them without a data teammate in the loop.

Sources indicate that this is a full-time individual contributor role for someone who likes being close to the business, enjoys turning messy operational data into numbers people trust, and is happy to work on both the models and the dashboards that sit on top of them. When Sales and Product have clear, reliable data, we help more creators build more valuable businesses with Kit.

You'll report to Sam Umachi, Head of Data (Linkedin).

Sales and RevOps are your primary partners, who will rely on the models and reporting you own. You'll also partner with our Product team on reporting for features like Visual Automations and on how creators use Kit.

Within our data team, you'll work alongside a Staff Analytics Engineer who owns org-wide semantic layer governance and modeling standards, a Senior Data Engineer who owns ingestion and pipelines, and a Senior Business Analytics Partner focused on revenue opportunities. This role has no direct reports.

First Week: Work through our onboarding curriculum in Notion and meet the data team, our Senior Revenue Operations Manager, the sales team, and your product partners. Get set up in our core tools: dbt Cloud, GitHub, Amazon Redshift, Omni, HubSpot, Linear, Hightouch and Slack. Set up your AI-assisted development environment and learn the shared AI workflows our data team uses. Open and merge your first small pull request so you learn our review and deployment flow early.

First Month: Map how HubSpot objects (deals, pipelines and stages, companies, contacts, and owners) flow into our dbt models, and document the gaps. Take over day-to-day ownership of the sales models and Omni dashboards that teammates have been covering. Audit current sales reporting and list where definitions differ or numbers don't reconcile. Get familiar with how commerce data (products creators sell and the revenue they earn through Kit) lands in the warehouse today. Agree with RevOps and Sales on the most notable questions they need answered. Review teammates' pull requests and contribute to our shared SQL, dbt, and documentation standards. Share a written reflection with the team on what you've learned and where you'd focus first.

It has been revealed that first Six Months: Ship and maintain well-tested, documented dbt models for core sales metrics, such as pipeline, deal velocity, stage conversion, win rates, and the sales-led funnel. Expose those metrics through the Omni semantic layer, working within the team's governance standards. Rebuild or refresh the core sales dashboards so pipeline reviews and forecasting conversations run on numbers that don't need manual reconciliation. Resolve competing sales metric definitions by writing down the options and tradeoffs, aligning with Sales and RevOps, and documenting the outcome. Model creator-level commerce data, such as products sold, revenue earned through Kit, and conversion, in partnership with data engineering. Write semantic layer descriptions, metric definitions, and documentation that let Omni's AI and MCP-connected AI tools answer routine sales questions correctly, and test them against real questions from Sales, RevOps and Product. Get Sales to the point where routine questions are answered through self-serve, whether in Omni dashboards, Omni's AI, or AI tools connected over MCP, rather than one-off requests.

First Year: Be the recognized owner of Kit's sales data, the person Sales and RevOps go to first and trust without second-guessing. Give our revenue analysis work the sales and commerce models it depends on, so deeper questions about pipeline health and creator earnings can be answered quickly, thereby enabling us to make creators more successful. Leave your domains well documented and well tested, legible to latest teammates, stakeholders, and the AI agents that query our semantic layer. Help raise the team's modeling quality through code review, pairing, and sharing what you learn.

Deep dbt experience. You build modular, tested, documented dbt projects, and you're comfortable with incremental models, snapshots, macros, CI, and scheduled jobs in dbt Cloud or similar.

Advanced SQL. You reason carefully about grain, joins, and window functions, and you write queries that are readable and performant on a cloud warehouse.

According to recent reports, data modeling for sales and GTM. You can model deals, pipeline stages and their history, ownership changes, and funnel conversion into clean, reusable structures. You are opinionated on Kimball standards and when a concept should be a fact or dimension.

It has been revealed that CRM data fluency. You know how sales data behaves in a CRM, including stage changes, backdated edits, and custom properties. HubSpot is preferred, but other CRM experience (e.g. Salesforce) applies just as well. We care most that you recognize common CRM patterns.

AI-assisted development. You use AI code editors and agents (such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or similar) every day, and you validate their output with tests, query results, and review before anything ships.

Clear written communication. You explain metric definitions, tradeoffs, and data caveats in plain language that Sales, RevOps, and Product partners understand.

BI and semantic layer experience. You can build dashboards and semantic models in Omni, Looker, or a similar BI tool, and you design metric definitions that people and AI tools can both query correctly.

Recent findings suggest that git-based workflows. You keep pull requests small and well described, and you give thoughtful code review.

Nice to have: Redshift performance tuning (sort and distribution keys), Python for scripting or API pulls, reverse ETL, and experience with product event, billing, payments, or ecommerce data.

Around 7 or more years in analytics engineering or data engineering where you personally shipped production data models.

Several years of hands-on work building and maintaining production dbt projects.

Working directly with sales teams and RevOps, and owning reporting they relied on to run the business.

Owning a data domain over time and evolving its models as the business and its questions changed.

In a recent development, working at a SaaS tech giant, ideally one with both a self-serve and a sales-led motion. Commerce, payments, or creator economy experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Working on a small or remote team where you were trusted to make decisions independently.

Recent findings suggest that ownership and follow-through. You treat your data domains as yours. You notice problems before stakeholders do, close the loop on requests, and finish what you start.

Judgment. You match rigor to the decision at hand, know when a quick answer is enough and when a request should become a durable model, and say so clearly.

Flexibility. You're glad to step outside your primary area when another team needs help, and you balance that work against your core commitments openly.

Recent findings suggest that teach everything you know. You document as you go, pair generously, and help stakeholders understand the data well enough to use it on their own.

Work in public. You share progress, open questions, and decisions in writing where the team can see them, including what didn't work.

Creator success is our success. You remember who's on the other end. A wrong number in a pipeline review means Sales spends time on the wrong creators, and that shapes how carefully you work.

According to recent reports, do it with excellence. You test your work, review it carefully, and don't ship a number you can't defend.

Candor with care. You're comfortable pushing back when a request won't answer the real question, and you do it in a way that builds trust.

Needing detailed specs or a highly structured environment before you can start.

Sources indicate that discomfort with ambiguity. Some of our sales and commerce definitions are still evolving, and you'll help settle them.

Needing several layers of approval to make modeling decisions within your domain.

Wanting to work only on dashboards, or only on pipelines, rather than across the transformation and BI layers.

Wanting a strictly fixed scope. Sales comes first, but you'll pick up Product or other work when the business needs it.

Wanting mostly greenfield work. Much of this role is improving sales models and dashboards that already exist.

Preferring to take tickets as written rather than partnering with stakeholders on what they need.

Being skeptical of AI's capabilities, or using AI without good judgment and accountability.

Expecting a large data team with dedicated specialists for every part of the stack.

Industry observers note that we're 100% remote with team members across the globe. We work mostly on East Coast time - so if you're based on the West Coast of the United States, Europe, or Asia, you might have a few early mornings or late evenings. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

Industry observers note that kit has standardized salaries based on position, no matter where you live. For this role, we're hiring at our level 4 ($172,000). Level is determined based on experience and our interview process.

We cover up to $2,280 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance aims through Aetna.

According to recent reports, $2,000 equipment allowance for your first two years, $1,000 budget every following two years. Manufacturer-provided laptops are issued to every Kit team member and are not included in the equipment budget.

Individual learning + development budget ($3,500/year).

Creator meetup budget ($50/month) to connect with creators over coffee, lunch, or other in-person meetups.

Childcare benefit up to $3,000 annually through JOON.

Twenty (20) days of paid time off during each year of employment.

Paid paid vacation: An after-tax bonus of $1,000 for taking five consecutive days of vacation where you’re fully unplugged from work.

Two weeks of paid sick time each year, including mental health + well being days.

Twelve (12) weeks paid parental leave and flexible scheduling in your child’s first year.

Up to six weeks of paid bereavement leave, medical leave, and disaster after six months of employment, two weeks of each paid leave in your first six months.

Sources indicate that winter Break Closure: Kit closes for a week at the end of December, giving everyone a collective break to enjoy the holiday season. Essential support services remain available, with teams coordinating to ensure coverage during this period.

Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team.

Fantastic in-person or virtual retreats with the team twice a year.

According to recent reports, we usually receive a large number of applications, and our goal is to follow up with you within two weeks. You’ll hear from us either way. Here’s what you can expect from the rest of our hiring process:.

A phone screen with our recruiter (30 min).

Hiring manager interview (45 min).

In a recent development, we’ll keep you informed through every step. To get started, complete this application, including a cover letter and answers to the questions on the next page. We read every single application, and your cover letter and responses help put your experience into context.

Kit is an equal opportunity employer.

Recent findings suggest that we value diversity in all of its forms. Research tells us that applicants who are female or non-binary, as well as applicants who are people of color, are less likely to apply for roles they do not feel 100% qualified for. If you think you meet more than 50% of our requirements but fewer than 100% of them, please apply.

We’re imperfect communicators, so think of our job postings as the starting point for discussion rather than proof that you shouldn’t apply.

Kit does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Substantial Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.
  • Industry observers note that well, according to Bloomberg, the current strategy is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OK, so Netflix failed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.

What if it bought NBCUniversal, tho?

That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Substantial Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.

Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

Industry observers note that well, according to Bloomberg, the current strategy is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses. The streamer first unveiled these in 2023, with a demo setup that looked like someone stocked the gift shop in Jurassic Park with merch of the laser murder doll from Squid Game.

At the time, Josh Simon, Netflix’s then-VP of Consumer Products (now CEO of collectibles company Funko) said the concept for Netflix Houses came from knowing “fans love to immerse themselves in the world of our movies and TV shows,” and “thinking a lot about how we take that to the next level.”.

Industry observers note that netflix had flirted with pop-ups before that; those were mainly focused on selling stuff. Make no mistake, Netflix Houses are also focused on selling stuff, but in a Disney World kind of way, where fans pay $39 to enter the House and head through an art gallery-esque space filled with themed exhibits like exclusive theater indicates, movie/TV set recreations, VR experiences, and arcade games. There are cafeterias and merch shops, but by and large the things to buy share billing with things to do.

The Houses are permanent installations (for now just in Dallas and Philly, with one planned to open in Vegas in 2027) but the exhibits within rotate regularly to keep up with whatever’s trending on Netflix.

It has been revealed that this year, for example, the Houses were renovated to feature animated smash megahit KPop Demon Hunters. They’ve also spotlighted Stranger Things, One Piece, Wednesday, and the aforementioned Squid Game.

Sources indicate that per Bloomberg, Netflix initially planned to open dozens of Houses across the U.S., focusing on quieter suburban areas away from downtowns. It wanted to snap up spaces in malls, which are not doing very well and might be willing to rent for cheap.

But apparently the results from its first two Houses haven’t been quite what Neflix expected, so it’s pausing openings beyond Vegas until it can reassess.

It has been revealed that people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the Philadelphia location has daytime draws like mini golf and a movie theater, but doesn’t see much traffic at night. Dallas, meanwhile, is breaking even financially, and has done well with larger groups and corporate events.

Recent findings suggest that netflix is also planning to see what comes from its Las Vegas location. Vegas, as you may know, is not in fact a quieter suburban locale–so if the House there proves to be profitable, with more traffic than Dallas and Philly, Netflix could reconsider where it opens in the future.

People familiar with the matter remarked Netflix is also looking at maybe taking Houses overseas. But wherever the next one ends up, it probably won’t open for at least another year, they said, until significant data from all three flagship U.S. locations is in.

Now, with all this in mind, it’s worth remembering Netflix just shock-fired its longtime Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria and replaced her with Peter Rice, Disney‘s former General Entertainment Chairman. Film chief Dan Lin is out too. Clearly, Netflix hopes to revamp more than its IRL installations…and perhaps it’s hoping Rice’s Disney EXP comes in handy with the Houses?

Four and a half years after winning a Grammy for The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical, the songwriting duo known as Barlow & Bear has something upcoming in store for TikTok viewers.

It has been revealed that abigail Barlow and Emily Bear are two of the creators behind To Die For Love, an 81-episode musical microdrama co-produced by TikTok and Ampersand. According to TikTok, the series follows “an ambitious half-witch vying for her coven’s crown. When she falls for a mortal, their romance takes an unexpected turn, forcing an impossible choice between family and the love of her life.”.

Barlow & Bear created an original score for To Die For Love, while Barlow co-wrote the script alongside Oscar-nominated writer/director, actor, and opera singer Julia Aks.

Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, barlow also stars in the series opposite Broadway vet Derek Klena. Executive producers include Ampersand CEO Agnes Chu, Benj Pasek, Justin Paul, Danielle Perelman, Chris Crema, Matthew Ko, and Kevin Weaver.

“Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear stated. “We love a pressure cooker, and building an entire musical in under five months proved that meaningful storytelling isn’t about time—it’s about the story and the people bringing it to life.”.

This isn’t the first creator-driven microdrama TikTok has brought to life. Earlier this year, Issa Rae’s media company, HOORAE, struck a deal with the platform to produce short-form web series for both TikTok and its companion app PineDrama. The first vertical series to emerge from that partnership, Screen Time, had racked up over 620 million views on TikTok and PineDrama as of late October, making it both platforms’ most-viewed show to date.

TikTok doubled down on that success last month when it announced a new microseries-focused partnership with Made By Us Studios, which describes itself as a “first-of-its-kind, Hollywood-grade studio designed for the creator economy and powered by creator management company MADE BY ALL.”.

Now, TikTok is forging ahead into the world of musical microdramas. To Die For Love will be available exclusively on TikTok and PineDrama, with all 81 episodes premiering December 21. The original soundtrack will be released by Atlantic Records.

Marketers will spend $116B on creators in 2026. They’re “cannibalizing” other budgets to do it.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (476 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.
  • According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.
  • Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.

According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.

Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.

Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

Madison and Wall compiled its study by isolating marketing funds dedicated to “creator related activity” (i.e., “spending deployed to creators, agencies, platforms, technology vendors, and media networks to achieve marketing, commerce, or brand objectives”). Other forms of creator income—such as subscriptions, merch, and platform payouts—weren’t taken into account.

The report further separated creator marketing spend into five distinct categories: audience-led spend, media-led spend, asset-led spend, infrastructure-led spend, and miscellaneous.

Of those categories, Madison and Wall found that media-led spending—aka “the paid amplification of creator content”—accounts for the largest piece of the pie at 44% (or $52 billion) of 2026 spend.

Audience-led spending (“the traditional sponsored-post and ambassador model”) ranks second at 28%, while asset-led spending (“where brands pay for content rather than reach”) accounts for 12% of the market. Infrastructure-led spending (net revenue kept by agencies, managers, and platforms) and miscellaneous (events, gifting, licensing, etc.) bring up the rear at 8% and 7% respectively.

It has been revealed that on a global scale, Madison and Wall found that the U.S. was responsible for 43% of creator spending in 2025, well above its ~35% share of global advertising. The closest runners-up were the UK (which accounts for 5% of global creator spending) and Germany (4%).

One of the key takeaways of Madison and Wall’s report concerned the origin of marketing funds dedicated to creator advertising.

Industry observers note that the firm noted that “creator growth is largely funded by reallocation rather than latest money. Interviews with stakeholders across the ecosystem point to three sources: traditional media, notably TV; digital performance media, including paid social, programmatic and search; and creative production budgets. Because creators draw on several existing budget pools at once, the creator economy can keep outgrowing advertising without marketers creating new budgets.”.

One senior operations executive told Madison and Wall that “80% of the time we are cannibalizing another budget, whether it’s TV or [something else].”.

Overall, the firm found that creator spending grew at an 18% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) between 2020 and 2025, as compared with 12% for advertising.

That gap doesn’t seem likely to close anytime soon. According to the firm’s projections, creator spending is set to grow ~12% a year through 2030—putting it well ahead of the 6% growth expected for the advertising economy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTube has come under fire in the past for how it handles content posted by people suspected of heinous crimes, but its policy has remained the same: It will only terminate a channel if someone is convicted in a court of law, and if their YouTube content is directly related to their crime.

    Now, the platform has refused a request from the Prison Service of England and Wales to remove content from Russell Brand‘s channel.

    The comedian and actor will be in prison for over a decade after being convicted of three counts of sexual assault and one count of rape, stemming attacks on four different women. Presiding British High Court judge Mr Justice Bennathan described Brand as a “sexual predator” whose behavior demonstrated a “series of lies” and “staggering arrogance.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    In the upload, Brand asserts innocence, telling viewers, “As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”.

    Authorities contacted YouTube via “an established mechanism the prison service has with tech companies to request deletion of material,” per the BBC, to ask that Brand’s video be removed.

    But YouTube isn’t willing to scrub it–at least not yet.

    Sources indicate that “We are aware of the new content and our teams are investigating,” a spokesperson from YouTube parent Google told the BBC. “We suspended Russell Brand’s channel from the YouTube Partner Program in September 2023. The channel has not been able to monetize on YouTube since then.”.

    It has been revealed that that’s a pretty typical order of operations for YouTube. In past cases with creators like Adnan Ahmed, Austin Jones, and Ian Rylett, YouTube suspended monetization on their channels when allegations surfaced and the legal process began, and then terminated their channels once convictions were filed.

    He also holds Christianity-themed “Sunday services” with Gallacher.

    Sources indicate that the assaults Brand was convicted for all happened before 2009; he made his YouTube channel in 2007, but didn’t start uploading videos until 2012. YouTube could potentially claim they’re not related based on timeline alone, since Brand–who was already a celebrity outside of YouTube–didn’t use his channel or digital clout to connect with his victims.

    So the question here is: Does YouTube amend its policies to ban convicted criminals–or specifically convicted sex offenders–from posting on its platform? What if their newly introduced content is directly related to their crimes, as Brand’s is?

    United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham got involved after YouTube’s initial denial, telling the platform (and other socmed platforms) to “show some decency and take these videos down.”.

    “[It’s] time that we focus on the victims and think about them,” he added, instead of “hearing from a convicted criminal.”.

    “I would call on those social media companies to take these interviews down,” Burnham added. “Why are we having to hear from him? We shouldn’t be, and certainly [victims] shouldn’t be hearing from him.”.

    The attention on YouTube’s refusal has sparked a bit of a Streisand effect. Commenters are flocking to Brand’s video, sneering at Burnham, the U.K. government, and activists for their attempts to remove it.

    “Had no intention to watch until the government told me not to,” one top-liked comment claims.

    “If the government tells you not to watch a video, you really need to watch that video to find out why,” another says.

    It has been revealed that other socmed platforms have cut Brand off. Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp–all owned by Meta–have culled his accounts, thanks to policies that prohobit convicted sex offenders from owning and/or operating accounts.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • YouTube was an official “Preferred Platform” for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and it worked to make the partnership a high scorer.
    • It also exercised the broadcast rights that came along with being a Preferred Platform: By the time Spain took it all home, YouTube’s World Cup content had drawn nearly 2 billion unique viewers, 550 million of whom tuned in from their TV sets and bumped YouTube’s Nielsen numbers.
    • But that success apparently isn’t enough of a carrot for YouTube to go bigger and bid for TV rights to future World Cups.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTube was an official “Preferred Platform” for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and it worked to make the partnership a high scorer. It tapped creators to film promo content, then brought them pitchside to film dozens of videos at the tournament’s top matches around the world.

    It also exercised the broadcast rights that came along with being a Preferred Platform: By the time Spain took it all home, YouTube’s World Cup content had drawn nearly 2 billion unique viewers, 550 million of whom tuned in from their TV sets and bumped YouTube’s Nielsen numbers.

    But that success apparently isn’t enough of a carrot for YouTube to go bigger and bid for TV rights to future World Cups.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to Atlantic sports columnist Andrew Marchand, YouTube declined to submit a bid for American broadcast rights to the 2030 and 2034 World Cups.

    There were rumors that YouTube planned to go out for rights, but a source familiar with the matter confirmed to Marchand that YouTube is not tossing its hat in the ring.

    It’s not alone: Apple, ESPN, NBC, and the newly formed Skydance have also declined to bid. Between their various subsidiaries, that knocks out chances of the World Cups airing on CBS, TNT Sports, Paramount+, HBO Max, and Telemundo.

    It has been revealed that so who does want the rights? Marchand reports Fox–which had the rights for 2026–is going out for them. But, perhaps surprisingly, the other top frontrunner seems to be Netflix.

    Or maybe it’s not so surprising–Netflix already has rights to the 2027 Women’s World Cup, and we know it’s willing to pay major for exclusive sporting events, so maybe the men’s Cup is exactly the complement it’s looking for.

    We don’t know what the winner will end up paying here, but Fox paid $485 million to air the 2026 tourney in the U.S. Netflix did say it expects to close out the year spending money on developing original content and investing in sports (and now it has freer cash considering its failed bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery). The World Cup just might be one of those investments.

    An offshoot of the long-running Clio Awards, which introduced in 1959 to honor excellence in advertising around the world, the Clio Creator Awards are presented by YouTube and backed by Influential, the content creator-led marketing organization Publicis Groupe bought for $500 million in 2024.

    The first Clio Creator event brought host Terry Crews to the Dolby Theater in Los Angeles to hand out awards in categories like Creator & Brand Collaborations, Public Relations, Integrated Campaign, and Written Content.

    “Creators aren’t just participating in culture, they’re shaping it,” Nicole Purcell, CEO of the Clios, stated in a statement. “The inaugural Clio Creator Awards recognize the incredible talent and originality driving this industry forward, from creators building their own communities to brands finding fresh ways to connect with audiences.     Creator x brand collabs have gotten nods in other ad industry events and award highlights (including Tubefilter’s own Streamy Awards)–but the fact that a legacy show like the Clios are embracing the creator world, and that these awards are backed by a Publicis Groupe subsidiary, points to further enmeshing of our space with traditional entertainment.

    Have you heard? GTA’s $3.79B day, e.l.f.’s record-breaking GRWM, and OnlyFans’ upcoming hire.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Each week, we handpick a selection of stories to give you a snapshot of trends, updates, business moves, and more from around the creator industry.
    • This week, GTA VI is making billions, a heartwarming viral moment is becoming a Lifetime movie, and TikTok wants you to know it’s a major deal in the music biz.
    • Topper Guild is getting into the animation game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Each week, we handpick a selection of stories to give you a snapshot of trends, updates, business moves, and more from around the creator industry.

    This week, GTA VI is making billions, a heartwarming viral moment is becoming a Lifetime movie, and TikTok wants you to know it’s a major deal in the music biz.

    Topper Guild is getting into the animation game. Content creator Topper Guild is teaming up with animation tech giant Toonstar to create an original series, which is set to premiere on YouTube. “Animation is a medium I’ve always wanted to work in, but I didn’t think it was possible to maintain that same pace my fans expect, or retain the creative control I have with my live-action content,” Guild remarked. “But Toonstar changed that. They’re unlocking animation for the creator economy.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Kane Parsons is going from Backrooms to BAFTA. YouTuber-turned-filmmaker Kane Parsons has been named as one of 14 creatives participating in BAFTA North America’s 2026 Breakthrough US cohort. The Backrooms director will join the program alongside rising entertainment icons like Heated Rivalry’s Connor Storrie and The ‘Burbs creator Celeste Hughey.

    Recent findings suggest that entrepreneurs On Fire has been acquired. John Lee Dumas has reportedly agreed to sell the firm behind his business podcast, Entrepreneurs On Fire, to PR firm Pathos Communications for $3 million in cash, plus up to $6 million in “performance payments.” Dumas will continue to host the show as part of a three-year deal.

    Industry observers note that youTube could pay billions over child safety concerns. Sources familiar with the matter reportedly told Bloomberg that YouTube is preparing to settle a wave of lawsuits regarding its allegedly “addictive” design by paying roughly $3 billion to thousands of school districts.

    TikTok dropped some major stats in its 2026 Music Impact Report. According to a study commissioned by TikTok from Luminate, 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 last year went viral on TikTok first—a ten-percentage-point jump from 2024. The report also noted that songs “that go viral on TikTok spend four times longer on the Billboard Global 200 than those without a viral moment.”.

    A Meta vet is coming to OnlyFans. Whitney Rosenthal is coming aboard as OnlyFans’ first global head of creator partnerships. The exec previously worked at Meta and YouTube; most recently, she served as vice president of global creator podcast platforms at Podimo.

    Streaming platforms are going all in on creator content. Upcoming data from Ampere Analysis indicates that U.S. streaming services debuted over 3,700 hours of “creator-led programming” in Q3 2026, up from 1,934 in the previous quarter. Distribution of new creator-led content on SVOD services also rose 75% over the last quarter, with Amazon Prime Video alone contributing over 230 hours (per Net Influencer).

    GTA VI made billions on day one. Rockstar Games announced Friday that Grand Theft Auto VI hit $3.79 billion during its first day of retail sales, “setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.”.

    Industry observers note that A microdrama studio will produce content for Black audiences. NBCUniversal and HarbourView Equity Partners are throwing their financial weight behind June, a microdrama studio debuted by Will and Dom Packer. The studio will focus on the development, production, and acquisition of original vertical dramas aimed at Black viewers.

    According to recent reports, freeman & Forrest has a upcoming majority owner. Falfurrias Management Partners has made a majority investment in B2B influencer marketing firm Freeman & Forrest. Co-founder Emily Freeman will stay on board as CEO, while co-founder Forrest Brazeal will continue in his role as president.

    Sources indicate that e.l.f. set a world record at TwitchCon. e.l.f. Cosmetics made history at TwitchCon 2026 by breaking the Guinness World Record for most people applying make-up simultaneously. The beauty brand’s massive GRWM included 733 in-person participants—and that was only the start of e.l.f.’s onsite activations at the con.

    According to recent reports, lifetime is turning a viral friendship into a film. In 2016, Wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton spread holiday cheer across the internet by sharing the heartwarming story of how an accidental text turned into an invitation to Thanksgiving dinner. Ten years later, Dench and Hinton have turned their shared Thanksgivings into an annual tradition—and now, Lifetime is turning it into a movie.

    According to recent reports, the Denver Broncos are tapping into the power of anime. The anime horse girls of Umamusume: Pretty Derby have become a familiar sight for sports fans in recent months, with appearances at events ranging from Grand Prix de Paris to Japan’s Super GT championship. Now—as part of an official collaboration with the Denver Broncos—two of the anime’s most recognizable characters will be on hand to support the team at Empower Field when they face the Miami Dolphins next month.

    Product Manager - Postgres at Supabase

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • We're hiring a Product Manager to own Postgres itself at Supabase.
    • You'll work closely with our Postgres engineering teams and with the PM lead for Databases, who leads Multigres.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We're hiring a Product Manager to own Postgres itself at Supabase. Every Supabase project is a full Postgres database, and Postgres is the foundation that Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions run on. You'll own the product experience of the database: Postgres versions and upgrades, maintenance, observability, extensions and security.

    You'll work closely with our Postgres engineering teams and with the PM lead for Databases, who leads Multigres. You'll define the Postgres requirements that architecture must meet, and own how customers experience their database through that transition.

    Industry observers note that this role is ideal for someone who loves Postgres, sweats the details that make a database trustworthy, and is excited about improving the experience for millions of developers. Small improvements here compound across every project on the platform.

    Industry observers note that you'll own Postgres versions, upgrades and end-of-life. Which major and minor versions we support, how and when customers upgrade, and how we retire old versions. Your goal is to make upgrades routine rather than risky.

    In a recent development, you'll make maintenance predictable. You'll design how we schedule, communicate and run maintenance windows so customers stay informed and in control, and disruption is rare and expected.

    Industry observers note that you'll help developers understand their database. Query performance, metrics, logs and advisors: you'll own the path from "my database is slow" to the fix.

    You'll own our extension ecosystem. Which extensions we offer, how we evaluate and support fresh ones, and how we keep them working across versions.

    You'll own Postgres security. Roles and permissions, Row Level Security ergonomics, secure defaults, and how we respond to Postgres and extension CVEs.

    You'll talk to developers across the full spectrum, from indie developers on their first project to enterprises running critical workloads, and bring what you learn into every prioritization call.

    Sources indicate that you'll own the problem definition, requirements and success metrics for what we ship, such as upgrade success rate, the share of the fleet on supported versions, and time-to-diagnose for performance problems. You'll set the metric before the team builds, then track it after launch.

    You'll keep Engineering, Support and GTM aligned. You'll own the plan of record for what's coming, why, and in what order, and communicate version changes and deprecations clearly to customers.

    4+ years of Product Management experience on databases, developer tools or infrastructure, or equivalent depth as an engineer, DBA or founder moving into product. You're comfortable commenting on an architecture doc and advocating for the user when trade-offs are required.

    Know Postgres well, or another relational database well enough to ramp swiftly. You're comfortable reading EXPLAIN output and talking about replication, WAL, roles and extensions.

    Have shipped products where reliability and trust are the experience. You treat downtime and breaking changes as product problems, not just operational ones.

    In a recent development, write clearly. Your specs, announcements and deprecation notices leave little room for confusion.

    Build with what you own. You run queries, test upgrades and try extensions yourself, and form opinions through first-hand use.

    According to recent reports, use AI to move faster. You use AI tools to compress research, drafting and feedback synthesis so you spend more time on judgment calls.

    Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

    Worked on a managed database service.

    Ran Postgres in production: upgrades, tuning, incident response.

    Worked on database observability, performance tooling, or security and compliance products.

    Contributed to Postgres, its extensions, or the wider open-source community.

    Shipped something using Supabase.

    According to recent reports, we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Industry observers note that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are crucial to us.

    According to recent reports, once a year, the entire manufacturer gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    Recent findings suggest that we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Industry observers note that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    Industry observers note that we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome to our rundown of the most-watched branded YouTube videos of the week.

    We’re publishing this snippet of a larger Gospel Stats Weekly Brand Report in order to analyze sponsorship trends in the creator economy. Any video launched in tandem with an official brand partner is eligible for t he ranking.

    And–as the name up above would imply–all the data comes from Gospel Stats. If you’re interested in learning more about Gospel–and which brands are sponsoring what creators on YouTube–click here. You can also download our YouTube 2025 Sponsorship Landscape Report here.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Boxing, golf, and football reign supreme in this week’s Gospel Stats Weekly Brand Report, with sponsorships from DAZN, DraftKings, Lowe’s, and more.

    #1 I finally saw quantum physics with my own eyes… Channel: Veritasium Brand: Ground News Views: 19,817,457.

    In a recent development, it’s not every day you get to see someone push the boundaries of physics. Veritasium secures a regular spot in our top 5 with his science deep dives, and this one might be among his best yet.

    Even for working scientists, accessing equipment for quantum physics experiments can be a tough time–so the Veritasium team’s partnership with the Gravity Laboratory at the University of Nottingham allowed them to give the world a vicarious look at what happens to helium when you just don’t stop cooling it down.

    The Gravity Lab’s gear allowed Veritasium–and now, any YouTube viewer–to observe helium’s transformation into a superfluid in real time, and discuss how superfluidity can be applied in fields like astrophysics.

    These kinds of videos remind me the universe is pretty cool, and even when things aren’t so hot on Earth (metaphorically speaking), there are countless galaxies dancing around us, full of potential.

    Industry observers note that oh, also, this video is sponsored by Ground News, which compares various news sources and evaluates them for potential biases. Its sponsorships spiked in the leadup to the midterm elections, but even after Voting Day, we’re still seeing decent numbers: It paid for ~20 other videos this week.

    #2 Suprised My Daughter with A Fresh E-bike ?@EskuteUS #shorts Channel: BikeLife Mom Brand: ESKUTE Views: 18,467,608.

    And now for something completely different. Helmet cam e-biker BikeLife Mom secured spot #2 with a 26-second skit where she “surprises” her daughter with a new e-bike from Eskute. The Short’s keep-’em-watching twist is that Ma wants to test drive the new piece herself…and the “test drive” might just last forever.

    #3 I Stayed in Waterpark Hotels Channel: Ryan Trahan Brand: Shopify Views: 13,539,328.

    #4 OLED iPad Mini is The Most Apple Product Theyve Ever Appled Channel: Marques Brownlee Brand: dbrand Views: 12,191,952.

    Industry observers note that BONUS #3,259 A *Shoppy* Vlog | Target, Walgreens, Grocery Haul + Are we turning a corner?? Channel: Jessica Braun Brand: Govee Views: 77,094.

    According to recent reports, we go from Veritasium letting viewers do physics vicariously to Jessica Braun letting viewers shop vicariously. With Black Friday coming up, basically every store is trying to whet shoppers’ appetites, but the economy is tough right now, and not everyone can cut loose with a day of dropping dolla dolla bills.

    That’s not to say Braun’s vlog is an ultra-luxury haul. It’s an everyday trip around to Target, Walmart, and out for groceries. Her sponsoring brand is equally everyday: smart lighting tech giant Govee. Someone told me once that color-changing lightbulbs let you instantly paint a room any color you want, for free, and you know what? I’ve found that to be true–and cheap.

    Govee paid for a handful of videos this week, including one promising to help people level up their “boring Millennial” Christmas trees and another highlighting TV surround lights.

    …and there’s a lot more data where that came from. If you like our Weekly Top 5, you’ll love everything else Gospel has to offer.

    It has been revealed that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    Supabase is looking for a Dev Experiences and Community Lead (SF) to help grow and scale our developer community initiatives and industry event programs.

    According to recent reports, you’ll work closely with the Head of Global Events and Field Marketing to build programs that connect Supabase with developers and the broader ecosystem. This includes initiatives such as meetups, workshops, hackathons, and community activations that bring Supabase into the spaces where developers learn, build, and collaborate.

    As an early member of the events team, you’ll help shape how Supabase highlights up in person around the world while building the playbooks and frameworks that allow these programs to scale globally.

    This role sits within Field Marketing and works cross-functionally across Marketing, DevRel, Partnerships, Sales and Design to support programs that deepen developer engagement, strengthen ecosystem relationships.

    You will also support programming around Supabase Select, our flagship user conference, including partner and community programming connected to the event.

    We’re a lean, remote-first team, so this role requires someone who is comfortable operating independently, experimenting with newly introduced ideas, and helping build the systems that will power Supabase’s events program as it grows.

    Own and Scale Community Programs.

    Scale Supabase developer meetups, workshops, and hackathons globally.

    Partner with DevRel to align community events with product launches and developer education initiatives.

    Coordinate community meetups around major industry events and Launch Week.

    Support community programming connected to Supabase Select.

    Support the SupaSquad advocate network through community activations.

    Support Industry Event Activations.

    Support Supabase’s presence at conferences such as AWS re:Invent, KubeCon, Stripe Sessions, Dash, and other events.

    Coordinate developer-focused side events, meetups, and partner activations around major conferences.

    Collaborate with Partnerships on co-hosted events.

    Turn Experiments Into Scalable Programs.

    Build playbooks and frameworks for community and ecosystem programs.

    Identify opportunities to scale successful initiatives across regions.

    Standardizing event formats and processes as program grow.

    Collaborate Across the Events Team.

    Partner with the events team on logistics and execution for community programs.

    Support promotion and event readiness with Marketing.

    Help ensure strong attendee experiences and post-event follow-up.

    5–7+ years in field marketing, developer marketing, community programs or partner marketing.

    Experience working with developer communities or technical audiences.

    Strong project management and organizational skills.

    Comfortable collaborating cross-functionally.

    Curious about developer ecosystems and the communities around modern infrastructure.

    Able to manage multiple initiatives in a fast-moving environmentComfortable working remotely and independently.

    Willing to travel for events as needed.

    Experience supporting developer meetups, hackathons, or workshops.

    Experience with community-led growth or developer advocacy programs.

    Experience running ecosystem or partner-led event programs.

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    It has been revealed that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are vital to us.

    Sources indicate that we operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale.

    In a recent development, we are looking for a Product Builder to join the IDP & RPA pod. You will take real problems from customers, decide what is worth solving, and build and ship the solution yourself, using AI tools to get from idea to production quickly without lowering the bar.

    Product Building is how Camunda's Experience organization builds the applications people use on top of Camunda 8, such as Hub, Operate, and ProcessOS. Small pods of builders own a product area from customer problem to shipped change, with no hand-offs between product management, design, and engineering. We are setting this model up now, so you will help shape how it works.

    Industry observers note that the IDP & RPA pod builds how Camunda processes work with documents and legacy applications. With intelligent document processing (IDP), customers create extraction and classification templates in Camunda Hub and publish them so a process can use AI to turn invoices and other documents into structured data. With robotic process automation (RPA), customers integrate legacy applications that have no APIs, using Robot Framework scripts on a standalone RPA worker. The hard problems come with putting LLMs into customer processes: extraction quality, model and prompt choices, testing and trust, and working for AI agents as well as for people.

    Help shape product direction for IDP & RPA by combining customer input, usage data, and field feedback into clear priorities.

    Partner with the other builders and product strategy to turn problems into shipped features, using short written proposals and prototypes to align early.

    Make judgment calls with incomplete information within your scope and own the outcome.

    Communicate trade-offs and decisions clearly to stakeholders who don't live in the details the way you do.

    Use AI tools across the whole loop, from specs to prototypes to production-ready code, and hold a high bar for what you ship by reviewing and improving the output rather than accepting it.

    Build, test, and ship improvements to the IDP & RPA experience, reading errors and tracing problems far enough to give your pod useful context.

    Talk to customers and to support and customer success colleagues about how IDP is used and where it breaks, and turn what you learn into decisions about what to build next.

    Pick up customer incidents and trace them across Hub, the connectors, and the deployed process of the customer.

    Track what you ship against real outcomes and adjust when the data tells you to.

    Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

    This role is an existing vacancy.

    It has been revealed that we offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

    The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:.

    United States: $119,900.00 to $193,200.00.

    United Kingdom: £75,300.00 to £123,800.00.

    Singapore: S$148,900.00 to S$223,300.00Singapore:.

    Canada: C$127,300.00 to C$209,300.00.

    If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

    Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

    Industry observers note that we invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

    Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

    In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

    Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program introduces in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

    Financial Security: Retirement and pension intends (often with firm contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

    Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

    Sources indicate that AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here.

    ”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

    Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

    Industry observers note that please be aware that scammers may impersonate Camunda by reaching out about job opportunities. Camunda will only contact candidates from an email address ending in @camunda.com or @talent.camunda.com. We will never ask candidates for bank account details, checks, payment, or other sensitive financial information as part of our hiring process. If you receive a suspicious message, please do not respond, click any links, or share personal information.

    By opting in to SMS use, please be aware that:.

    Text message frequency may vary;.

    Standard text message and data rates may apply; and.

    By opting in, you will be enrolled directly in ongoing recruiting text messages from Camunda.

    Industry observers note that to opt-out, simply select 'No' when prompted during your application. You can also change your preferences at any time by contacting talent-operations@camunda.com.

    Vox rolls out its first app with an eye toward building paid memberships

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Niemanlab

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that all the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing.
    • We have sent a confirmation link to .
    • Vox users can watch videos and listen to podcasts in the app, but reading stories requires a paid subscription.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that all the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing. Our daily newsletter is a must-read from newsrooms to executive suites.

    We will never sell your address. Prefer a weekly email?

    Nearly there — check your email.

    We have sent a confirmation link to . Click it and you are on the list. If it has not turned up in a minute or two, it may be in your spam folder.

    Vox users can watch videos and listen to podcasts in the app, but reading stories requires a paid subscription.

    Vox has launched its first mobile application, the publication best known for its explanatory journalism declared Wednesday morning.

    Industry observers note that growing membership is a “key priority,” managing editor for audience and membership Bill Carey mentioned. Vox believes launching the app is one way to do that. A Vox membership costs $5 per month, or $60 per year, and offers ad-free versions of podcasts and unlimited access to all of the website’s contents.

    RELATED ARTICLEVox is revamping its editorial strategy to redefine what ‘Voxxy’ meansHanaa' TameezNovember 8, 2021Strengthening its relationship to its audience is only becoming more important for Vox. The app launch comes at a time when news publishers are increasingly trying to keep customers on their own platforms amid growing preferences for AI summaries, news creators, and industry-wide traffic declines.

    Industry observers note that “The move toward developing our membership program in the last couple of years has really been about understanding how important it is for us to build more community and to foster that loyalty [of our] audience,” Carey noted. “When we were looking at that, it really felt like an app was a good way to continue pointing in that direction.”.

    Vox isn’t the only news outlet focusing on mobile apps. The Verge — Vox’s former sister publication under Vox Media — named traffic declines as one of the reasons why it prepares to launch its own app next year. The Wall Street Journal’s head of digital, Taneth Evans, recently stated that the Journal makes its app more useful to users by offering all of its mediums in one place. Evans also said that news publishers “need to give people reasons to open an app beyond simply offering news.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Websites will become a service for agents,” Evans said. “Apps are gonna be the thing that humans will connect with.”.

    Vox declined to provide website traffic numbers, but data from Comscore highlights that the website’s unique visitors decreased by 36% year-over-year between September 2025 (7.4 million) and September 2026 (4.8 million). Archived data from SimilarWeb shows the site had 20.8 million visits in September 2021.

    “Vox isn’t immune to the larger trends that have led to web traffic declines in recent years, but those only represent a portion of our audience,” Carey mentioned in an email. “Vox is focused on building audience engagement across platforms, with social video views up 86% year-over-year and newsletter audience up 14%.”.

    “Even if there wasn’t a decline in search traffic, as everyone has been seeing — and we still get members from search — we want to create that relationship with our audience,” publisher and editor-in-chief Swati Sharma said. “People know Vox and they have a relationship with Vox. We have a younger audience that’s on all of these different platforms. I think it is definitely a part of building that relationship ourselves.”.

    That the app makes all Vox content accessible in one place for current and future members also signals the “un-siloing” of the newsroom overall, Sharma said. Vox right now has 78 editorial employees.

    Recent findings suggest that RELATED ARTICLESwati Sharma is leading a new era in Vox’s mission to “explain the world”Hanaa' TameezMay 6, 2021When Sharma, who has helmed Vox.com since 2021, first arrived, she found that Vox’s main mediums (text, audio, and video) “weren’t in service of one another.” The “silos” allowed teams to build their own audiences and products. But while teams discussed story ideas with each other and during editorial meetings, “they all [needed] to go into their creative spaces and find what works for their medium and not be in service of just one larger section.”.

    Sources indicate that that’s changed over the past five years, Sharma stated. Each team — text, video, and audio — does a little bit of everything now. Text reporters appear on podcasts and in videos, while podcasters and hosts also write their own newsletters.

    It has been revealed that “In a lot of newsrooms, there’s one dominant form, and at Vox, there wasn’t. They’re all really crucial,” Sharma noted. “[Senior correspondent] Dylan Scott is on our Unexplainable podcast talking about Alzheimer’s. [Host and editorial director] Astead Herndon does a newsletter and a Substack Live every week, and he does a podcast. That’s the future for us, and that’s where our whole newsroom is moving, where those silos are done and you can basically do everything.”.

    #55377. Breaking: Google Explains How To Avoid CDN Migration SEO Problems via @sejournal, @martinibuster

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Google Explains How To Avoid CDN Migration SEO Problems via @sejournal, @martinibuster

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1119 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Googlers Gary Illyes and Cherry Prommawin explain how moving to a CDN can unexpectedly increase crawling and overwhelm the origin server, despite eventually improving website performance.
    • Illyes and Prommawin explained that moving to a CDN can cause Googlebot to increase crawling because faster server responses signal that the site’s infrastructure can handle more requests.
    • CDN caches are initially empty and the CDN only starts caching when a browser or bot requests a page at which point the request has to be forwarded to the origin server, where the actual website is at.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Googlers Gary Illyes and Cherry Prommawin explain how moving to a CDN can unexpectedly increase crawling and overwhelm the origin server, despite eventually improving website performance. They also share that attempts to control crawler traffic can sometimes accidentally block Googlebot and harm Search visibility.

    Illyes and Prommawin explained that moving to a CDN can cause Googlebot to increase crawling because faster server responses signal that the site’s infrastructure can handle more requests. Google’s automated crawling systems interpret the improved performance as an indication that more crawling is possible and responds by gradually increasing the crawl rate.

    CDN caches are initially empty and the CDN only starts caching when a browser or bot requests a page at which point the request has to be forwarded to the origin server, where the actual website is at.

    When Google increases the crawl rate, the initial crawl is handled by the origin server. But now Googlebot is hitting the server more aggressively and it’s this that can overwhelm the origin server, initially.

    According to recent reports, “For one, suddenly the crawling metrics suggests the site can handle a larger amount of crawling. And on the flip side, because the CDN caches aren’t yet populated, the origin server still has to serve the requested pages.

    Basically, CDNs take the valve off the hose, so now crawlers are drinking from a fire hose.”.

    Cherry Prommawin added more details:.

    According to recent reports, “Under normal circumstances, our crawlers operate under an key rule. When a server responds faster, the crawlers assume the infrastructure is healthy and slowly ramp up crawl speed.

    …So the crawlers see how fast the server responds, get really excited, and start to crawl the entire site at a higher, higher, and higher speed. But it’s a trap.

    People assume a CDN can catch a crawl spike from day one, but …The cache has to be filled up with the assets off the site first.”.

    Gary Illyes explained that on a first request for a page the CDN has to fetch the page from the origin server first to populate the cache with the content. It’s not until the second request for the page that the cache is populated with the content and begins doing its job.

    “…which means your origin server may get slammed by the flood anyway. Now, to be fair, our crawlers take time to ramp up. It won’t happen in a millisecond.

    An empty cache means your origin server is still doing all the heavy lifting. Until that cache is populated, your CDN isn’t acting as a shield just yet.”.

    A CDN cannot serve an un-cached URL without retrieving it first from the origin server and that only happens after a request for that URL is first made. Crawlers visit large numbers of URLs virtually all the time and can generate a substantial amount of origin traffic before the CDN’s caches are fully populated.

    This next issue involves accidentally blocking Googlebot and triggering a reduced search presence because Google can no longer crawl and index URLs from a website. Illyes and Prommawin explain it in the context of a website admin flipping a switch at Cloudflare and inadvertently blocking Googlebot.

    This is a real problem, I recall an instance in which a popular website’s massive traffic dried up whenever Cloudflare was activated and would return once they turned it off. They had a devil of a time diagnosing why this was happening and the customer service people at the time were unable to help them. It may have been the case, as Illyes and Prommawin noted, that the admin had turned on a strict bot filter that inadvertently blocked Googlebot.

    Illyes offered an example of an admin doing exactly that:.

    “They look at the spiking traffic, assume they are being aggressively scraped by botnets, and naturally, they panic.”.

    And what sometimes happens next is that an admin might turn on “blanket security rules” that block Googlebot.

    Prommawin offered more details:.

    …If the CDN detects automated requests, it intercepts them with a CAPTCHA challenge, asking them to click pictures of traffic lights to prove they’re human.

    …It sees automated requests, flags it as a bot, and then intercepts with a CAPTCHA. And since our crawlers cannot identify a traffic light, they fail the test.”.

    What eventually happens with prolonged Googlebot blocking is that Google will begin dropping the pages from the index.

    In a recent development, prommawin suggested that site admins should configure their CDN to allow known and trusted crawlers. This is a method called whitelisting where only crawlers that are on the “allowed” list can get it and all other crawlers cannot.

    They also recommend the use of CDN-level rate limiting of Googlebot if the requests on the origin server lead to downtime which can negatively impact legitimate human traffic to the website.

    It has been revealed that when a site initially starts out with a CDN, the CDN does not have a cache of a website’s content. The cache doesn’t get loaded until it’s requested by a browser or crawler visit.

    Sources indicate that cache pre-warming is the process of requesting content from a site so that the content gets loaded onto the CDN. This ensures that the content is already loaded onto the CDN before users request it, which ensures that the content is delivered rapidly without the CDN having to first retrieve it from the origin server (the server where the actual content files exist).

    Illyes recommends “pre-warming” the cache by programmatically requesting URLs from it so that thE cache is populated in a controlled manner.

    “And to survive augmenting your site with a CDN, see if you can pre-warm the caches by programmatically fetching your top URLs through the CDN before you open the floodgates to search engines.”.

    Recent findings suggest that google’s main point is that moving to a CDN can create an unexpected combination of faster crawling and increased origin-server demand. That in turn can lead to unintentionally setting aggressive security restrictions that prevent Googlebot from accessing a website.

    Three especially crucial points for SEOs and site owners:.

    Sources indicate that 1. Using a CDN can trigger an increase in Googlebot crawling when it detects faster server responses, even though the CDN’s caches have not yet been populated, which in turn means an increase in requests for URLs from the origin server.

    According to recent reports, 2. A CDN migration can inadvertently cause pages to disappear from Google Search due to aggressive security settings intended to stop malicious bots can also lock out Google’s crawlers.

    3. Google recommends pre-warming caches, allowing trusted crawlers, and temporarily controlling crawling when server demand becomes excessive.
